name: Island Encore
vibe: By day the island is a pastel toy diorama. At 'Showtime' it becomes a neon stage for idols. Picture collectible vinyl toys standing on a candy-coloured stage set: chunky rounded shapes, soft 3-band cel shading with a glossy rim sheen, a cotton-candy sky and a turquoise sea with a bright foam ring around the island. The K-pop energy comes from how things are staged, never from copying anyone. That means sweeping spotlight beams, marquee bulbs, glow wands in each child's own signature colour, holographic photocard-style shop cards, confetti cannons, pet dance breaks in sync and a bouncy original soundtrack. Colour ratio rule: 70% soft pastels on surfaces, 20% clear mid-saturation colour on items and characters, and 10% neon on emissive accents only, mostly at Showtime. Holding to that ratio is what keeps it stylish to a parent instead of tacky. It needs to be cute enough for a 6-year-old (big-eyed pets, squishy bounces) and cool enough for a 12-year-old (night mode, chrome and holo finishes, kart under-glow, stage-cam camera moves, dance emotes). Everything stays friendly: tumbles are cartoon flips with dizzy sparkles, nothing breaks, and nobody loses badly.

lightingAndMaterials:
RENDERER (three r170): WebGLRenderer({antialias: tier !== 'LOW', alpha: false, stencil: false, powerPreference: 'high-performance'}). Set outputColorSpace = SRGBColorSpace and toneMapping = NeutralToneMapping, because it keeps pastel hues where ACES greys them. Exposure is 1.0 by day and 1.08 at Showtime. Lights are physically correct, which is the r170 default, so the intensities below are the real values to use. Pass every palette hex through new Color('#hex') and three handles sRGB to linear.

DAY PRESET: HemisphereLight(sky #DDF1FF, ground #FFE0EC, intensity 1.9). One DirectionalLight 'sun', #FFF3E0 at 2.4, positioned at (-7, 14, 9) and aimed at (0,0,0). That lights from the front-left, so faces toward the camera are lit and shadows fall back-right, matching the 2D art. No AmbientLight. Fog(#FFE3F1, near 30, far 70). Calibration: the lit grass top should read within ±6% lightness of #8EE07A on screen; tune only the sun intensity to get there.

SHOWTIME PRESET (dusk stage): Hemisphere sky #6B5BD6, ground #2A1840, intensity 0.85. The sun becomes a 'moon': #B9C6FF at 0.9, same direction. Rim colour changes to #FF7AD9, mixed 60/40 with the child's signature colour. All neon materials go to full, halo sprites grow to 1.6× size, the 3 spotlight cones turn on, the star field turns on, and Fog becomes (#3B1E6E, 24, 60). Transition: lerp every colour and intensity over 1.6 s with inOutSine. With reduced motion, crossfade in 0.25 s.

SHADOWS: MID and HIGH tiers only. sun.castShadow on, mapSize 2048 on HIGH and 1024 on MID, PCFShadowMap. The orthographic shadow camera is fitted to the island: left/right -10..10, top/bottom -7..7, near 1, far 40, bias -0.0004, normalBias 0.03. Set renderer.shadowMap.autoUpdate = false and set needsUpdate = true only after a change to layout, house style or day/night. The scene is static, so shadows then cost nothing per frame. Only static items cast shadows, and the ground receives them. Everything that moves (pets, avatar, swing seat, bubbles, confetti) uses a BLOB shadow instead: an instanced plane with a 64² radial texture, #3B2F4A at opacity 0.22, sized 0.9 × footprint, shrinking as the object rises. LOW tier uses blob shadows only.

MATERIAL SET: one factory, cached by palette token, at most 12 shader programs.
(1) TOON, about 90% of meshes. MeshToonMaterial({color, gradientMap: G}), where G is a 4×1 RedFormat DataTexture with values [110, 165, 215, 255], NearestFilter for min and mag, generateMipmaps false. Add a shared rim patch via onBeforeCompile, inserted before '#include <opaque_fragment>': outgoingLight += uRimColor * pow(1.0 - clamp(dot(normal, geometryViewDir), 0.0, 1.0), 2.5) * uRimStrength. All toon materials share one uniforms object, so a single write switches day and night. Set customProgramCacheKey = () => 'encore-toon' so every colour shares one program. Rim by day: #FFFFFF at strength 0.28. At Showtime: strength 0.55. Rocks use flatShading for a faceted gem look; everything else uses smooth normals.
(2) NEON. MeshBasicMaterial({color: neon token, toneMapped: false}) so it stays unlit and pops above tone mapping. Each neon tube is a core TubeGeometry (r 0.02, 4 radial segments) plus a 'glow sleeve' (r 0.06, MeshBasic, AdditiveBlending, depthWrite false), with opacity 0 by day and 0.45 at Showtime. By day, neon parts that are switched off show their pastel off-colour through the toon material (e.g. bulbs #FFF3B3).
(3) HALO sprites, a fake bloom. One 64² CanvasTexture with alpha = (1-r)^2, drawn as instanced billboard quads with AdditiveBlending, depthWrite false and a per-instance tint. Size 0.5–1.2 u; opacity 0.5 by day and 0.9 at Showtime. No post-processing by default. The only optional extra is UnrealBloomPass on HIGH: half resolution, strength 0.55, radius 0.35, threshold 0.9, and only when the device has been measured at ≥ 55 fps.
(4) PREMIUM METAL. MeshMatcapMaterial with 128² matcaps drawn on canvas at runtime. GOLD: radial #FFF6CC → #FFE89A at 30% → #F0C02F at 60% → #C9921A at 90% → #8A5F10 at the edge, plus a white spec dot at uv (0.35, 0.3). CHROME: #FFFFFF → #DDE3F0 → #9AA3B8, with a #C7B8FF iridescent edge. PEARL/HOLO: conic #FFB3E6 → #B3E5FF → #C9FFE5 → #FFF3B3.
(5) GLASS/BUBBLE. PEARL matcap, transparent, opacity 0.45, depthWrite false, rendered after opaque objects.
(6) WATER. One 80×80 plane with a ShaderMaterial. Colour = mix(#7FE3F0, #2F8FD8, smoothstep(0, 2.5, shoreDist)). Foam #F2FCFF where shoreDist < 0.12 + 0.06*sin(t*1.3 + shoreDist*9). Add 6 stylised wave-line bands (#E8F8FF at 0.5) scrolling at 0.04 u/s. shoreDist comes from a 64×40 distance texture baked on the CPU from the land cells; re-bake it when land unlocks. At Showtime: shallow #3C6FD1, deep #1B2A6B, foam #CFC4FF, plus additive pink and cyan streaks where the spot cones meet the water. By day only, add 40 instanced twinkle glints.
(7) SKY. An inverted sphere (r 90, 24×12 segments) with a ShaderMaterial, fog false and depthWrite false, using a 3-stop vertical gradient. Day: #8FD3FF → #CDEBFF → #FFE3F1. Showtime: #1A1240 → #3B1E6E → #FF7AC8. 4–5 cloud puffs, each 3–5 merged icospheres in white toon with rim, drift at 0.08 u/s. At Showtime, add a star field of 250 Points (120 on LOW), size 2 px with sizeAttenuation false, twinkling slowly in the shader (sin(t*2 + id)).
(8) SPOTLIGHT CONES, Showtime only. ConeGeometry(1.3, 10, 16, 1, openEnded) with an additive ShaderMaterial, alpha = 0.2 * (1 - vUv.y)^1.4 with soft edges. Colours are Neon Pink, Neon Cyan and Neon Violet. They are mounted on 2 decorative 'stage buoys' in the sea at the back corners and on one point behind the house. They sweep ±25° at 0.12 Hz with phases 120° apart. These are NOT real SpotLights.
(9) OUTLINE, hero objects on MID and HIGH only. Inverted hull: MeshBasicMaterial(#3B2F4A, side BackSide), with 'transformed += normal * uOutline' added after '#include <begin_vertex>'. uOutline is 0.018 u for buildings and attractions and 0.012 u for pets, avatar and accessories. In edit mode the selected item's hull turns #FFD23F and pulses 0.018↔0.03 u at 1.5 Hz.

EXTRAS: lanterns, mushrooms and the lighthouse, when switched on at Showtime, cast an additive ground decal (radius 0.7, their own colour, opacity 0.35). House windows glow #FFE9A8 (MeshBasic) at Showtime.
modellingRules:
UNITS AND AXES: 1 grid cell = 1.0 world unit (about 1 m at toy scale), Y up. Grid cell (c, r) has its centre at x = c - 7.5, z = r - 4.5. +z points toward the default camera, so row 9 is nearest, the same as the bottom of the 2D map. A placed item with fp [w, h] at (x, y) pivots on its footprint centre (x + w/2 - 8, 0, y + h/2 - 5), with its base at y = 0 (top of the grass). Models face +z. Sea level is y = -0.32. The grass slab runs from 0 down to -0.35. The sand skirt's top is at -0.12 and it reaches 0.25 beyond the grass. Keep a 0.07 u margin inside each footprint so models fit in 0.86 × 0.86 per cell and neighbours never intersect. Only tree canopies above y = 1.0 may overhang, up to 1.1 u wide.

REFERENCE HEIGHTS (u): path 0.04 | flowers 0.35–0.6 | rose bush 0.6 | rock 0.45 | bench 0.5 | sandcastle 0.7 | snowman 0.95 | umbrella 1.25 | oak 1.6 | apple 1.55 | blossom 1.6 | pine 1.8 | palm 1.9 | lantern 1.4 | mushrooms 0.55 | flag pole 1.9 | bunting 1.0 | windmill 2.2 | lighthouse 2.8 (tallest decor) | trampoline 0.45 | fountain 0.95 | swing 1.4 | bubble machine 0.8 | house 2.3 at the ridge (castle turrets 2.9) | course gate 1.9 | garage 1.4 | pitch stand 0.4 | pets 0.5–0.6 to the top of the head (dragon 0.65) | 'you' avatar 0.95.

SHAPE LANGUAGE ('soft vinyl toy'): about 80% curves, built only from this primitive kit:
- puff(r) = IcosahedronGeometry(r, 1), or a sphere 12×8
- bean(r, len) = CapsuleGeometry(r, len, 3, 10)
- slab(w, h, d) = RoundedBoxGeometry from three/addons, segments 2, radius 0.18 × the smallest side
- tube(r, h) = CylinderGeometry with 12 radial segments
- drop(r, h) = LatheGeometry of an 8-point profile with 10 segments (tulips, mushroom caps, round-tipped cones)
- ring(R, r) = TorusGeometry 16×6
- star(5 points, rOut, rIn) = ExtrudeGeometry, depth 0.25·rOut, bevel 0.3·depth, bevelSegments 2 (puffy stars)
- flag(w, h) = PlaneGeometry with 8×1 segments
- ribbon = TubeGeometry along a CatmullRomCurve3 with 4 radial segments
Proportions are chunky, about 1.2× thicker than real. Heads are big: a pet's head is about 45% of its height. Minimum part thickness is 0.02 u. Ropes are 0.012 u with 4 radial segments, and whiskers are LineSegments.

TRIANGLE BUDGETS: path tile ≤ 120 | flower patch ≤ 350 (instanced petals) | small decor ≤ 500 | trees ≤ 900 | windmill and lighthouse ≤ 1,400 | fun items ≤ 1,200 | house with all details ≤ 3,500 | each attraction ≤ 4,000 (plus ≤ 2,000 for an instanced crowd) | pet ≤ 1,800, plus ≤ 300 per accessory | avatar ≤ 1,500 | game kart ≤ 1,500 plus its driver. On the LOW tier, cut segment counts by 30% (spheres 10×6, cylinders 8).

COLOUR AND SHADING: use palette tokens only, plus the LOCKED style colours already in world-art.js and the game files (WALL, DOOR, roof pairs, PETCOL, KARTS, BALLS, STADIA, THEME, the course THEMES, the kart TRACKS grass). Each object uses at most 3 tones from one colour family: base, shade (-12% lightness, on undersides and secondary parts) and highlight (+12% lightness, as a dab at the top-left). An item has at most 4 materials. After building, merge parts per material with BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries, giving at most 4 meshes per item.

STRUCTURE: one factory per id, build(id, state, tier), returns a Group with named pivots that the act handlers drive:
- 'sway': whole-item idle
- 'spin': windmill sails, stars
- 'swing': swing seat
- 'flag': cloth
- 'glow': lamp parts and halo
- 'water': jets
- 'emitter': bubbles and smoke
- 'door'
- 'hat', 'neck', 'face', 'back': pet accessory sockets
- 'seat': kart driver
Repeatables (paths, and decor bought in multiples) render as one InstancedMesh per (id, material part). Animated sub-parts such as cloth and sails live in a separate small InstancedMesh that updates every frame. Static instances are never touched after placement.

DETERMINISTIC CHARM: hash each placed uid to a yaw jitter of ±8° and a scale of 0.94–1.06 for organic decor (trees, flowers, bushes, rocks, mushrooms). NEVER jitter the house, attractions, paths or fun items; the grid has to stay tidy and editable.

LOOK TABLE (testable): put per-id look data in a pure data module with no THREE import (e.g. world/world-look.js). It holds height, palette tokens, part list, act pivot names and Showtime behaviour. A Node test can then check that every CATALOG id has a look and that it uses only palette or locked tokens. The THREE builders read from that table.

HIT VOLUMES: every tappable item gets an invisible raycast box of footprint × max(height, 0.8 u) so small fingers hit it. Pets get a 0.8 u sphere. Raycast only against these boxes, never against the meshes.
itemCategoryNotes: ISLAND GROUND / SEA / SKY (applies everywhere): Land is one InstancedMesh of slab(1.02, 0.35, 1.02) grass tiles with tops at y 0, sitting over a second InstancedMesh of slab(1.5, 0.22, 1.5) sand tiles with tops at -0.12. The large overlap melts the cells into one blobby landmass, the same way the 2D art does. Grass tops alternate #8EE07A and #84D872 in a faint checker. Slab sides are #5FBF55. Sand is #F3DC9A with a wet-sand ring of #E8C77E at the waterline. Add 1–2 instanced grass tufts per open cell (3 crossed blade planes, #4FA94A), placed deterministically per cell. Sea, sky, clouds, stars and stage buoys follow the lighting section. The turquoise sea and bright foam ring around the island are the most important first impression, so build and polish them first.

TREES (tree_oak, tree_pine, tree_apple, tree_blossom, tree_palm). No act. Idle sway on the 'sway' pivot with phase taken from uid: oak, apple and blossom 1.5° every 4.2 s; pine 1° every 5 s; palm 3° every 3.6 s.
- oak: trunk tube tapering from r 0.12 to 0.08, h 0.7, #9B6B43. Canopy is 3 puffs: r 0.44 in #5CB85C on top, two r 0.36 in #4BA84B lower down. A highlight dab of r 0.16 in #8BD17C sits top-left. Total height 1.6.
- pine: trunk #8A5D3A, h 0.3, under 3 stacked round-tipped cones of r 0.48, 0.38 and 0.26 in #3F9A5A; the top cone is #69C07C. Height 1.8.
- apple: the oak canopy plus 6 apples, each puff(0.06) in #E53935 with a white spec dot. Height 1.55.
- blossom: the oak shape in #F6A7C8, #EC86B0 and #FFD3E6. 3–4 petal quads per tree drift down and respawn (#FFD3E6, at most 40 on the island).
- palm: trunk is 6 short tubes stepping along a curve in alternating rings of #A5743F and #8A5A2B. 5 drooping flattened-bean fronds in #4FBF63, #45B05A, #5CCC70 and #3FA956, plus 2 coconuts in #8A5A2B. Height 1.9.

FLOWERS AND PLANTS (flower_tulip, flower_daisy, flower_sun, bush_rose, rock_mossy). Every patch sits on a low mound, slab(0.7, 0.08, 0.5) in #4FAE4C. Idle: flower heads bob ±2% in scale every 2.4 s.
- tulip: 3 stems (r 0.015, h 0.28–0.38, #3C8A3C). Cups are drop(0.06, 0.1) in #FF5C6C, #FFC93C and #FF7AB8, with one bean leaf.
- daisy: 5 daisies, each 8 instanced white petals (flattened beans 0.05 long) around a #FFC93C centre, tilted 25° toward the camera.
- sunflower: 2 flowers, 0.75 and 0.6 u tall, each a #8A5A2B disc of r 0.09 with 12 petals in #FFCF2E. The heads slowly turn toward the sun by day, and at Showtime they swivel to follow the sweeping spotlight. That honours the shop text 'follow the sun'.
- rose bush: 3 puffs in #3F9A4A and #4CAF50 with 6 layered rose buds in #FF7AA8, #FF5C8A and #FF9DBF.
- mossy rock: a flat-shaded Dodecahedron (r 0.32, #A9A6B8, scaled 1 / 0.62 / 0.85) with a moss cap: a squashed #6CC26A puff over the top 40%. To match 'friendly', give it two tiny ink dot eyes that blink every 5–9 s, so it reads as a shy rock friend.

LIGHTS (lantern, mushroom_glow). Act 'glow' toggles them on and off, and the on/off state persists as it does today.
- lantern: post tube (r 0.04, h 1.05, #4B4F6B) on a slab base. Lamp cage is slab(0.26, 0.3, 0.26); the glass is #CFE0EC when off and #FFE36B MeshBasic when on. Inside is a puffy star bulb (r 0.07), a nod to a glow wand. A 4-sided cone cap. When on: #FFF6A8 halo of 0.9 u, plus a pool of light on the ground at Showtime. Switching on runs 3 gentle flicker steps over 0.25 s (not a strobe) and plays 'star'.
- mushroom_glow: 3 mushrooms with bean stems in #FFF4E0 and drop caps of r 0.13, 0.17 and 0.10, with white puff spots. Caps are #B06BD8 when off and #6FF3FF neon when on, with a #9FFCFF halo. When on and music is playing, the caps pulse ±12% on each beat.

FLAGS AND PARTY (flag_pole, bunting). Act 'wave'. At Showtime both pick up tiny neon LED dots along their edges, twinkling at no more than 1.5 Hz.
- flag_pole: pole tube (r 0.03, h 1.9, #8F8AA6) with a puff finial in GOLD matcap. Cloth is a 0.7×0.45 plane with 8×1 segments, #FF6B6B with a #FFD23F diamond. Idle flutter is a sine wave on the CPU (0.04 u, 2 Hz) that grows toward the free edge. On tap it flutters harder (0.12 u for 1.2 s) and plays 'whoosh'.
- bunting: 2 posts (r 0.03, h 1.0, #9B6B43) with a sagging ribbon line between them. 5 pennants hang from it in #FF6B6B, #FFD23F, #4FC3F7, #7BD88F and #C38BFF, swinging ±6° with staggered phases. On tap a ripple runs along the line from left to right in 0.6 s.

GARDEN AND BEACH DECOR (bench, sandcastle, umbrella, snowman).
- bench: 2 seat planks and 2 back planks, each slab(0.8, 0.06, 0.12) in #C48A52, on #6B5A7A legs. At Showtime an idle pet nearby may hop up and sit.
- sandcastle: in #F2CD7C. A central keep (tube r 0.18, h 0.45) and 2 towers (r 0.11, h 0.55) with 4-tooth crenels, a #C99A4D door arch, a #FF6B6B flag on a 0.25 u stick, and #FFD3E6 shell dots.
- umbrella: canopy is an 8-segment cone (r 0.55, h 0.25) with wedges alternating #FF6B6B and #FFFFFF via vertex colours, tilted 8°. Pole #8F8AA6, with a #4FC3F7 towel slab beside it.
- snowman: puffs of r 0.22 and 0.16 in #FDFDFF (the rim light makes them glow softly). #3B2F4A top hat, a drop() carrot in #FF8A3D, a torus scarf in #FF5C6C with a tail, and ink coal dots. 6 slow snow sparkles drift around him, because he 'never melts'.

LANDMARKS (windmill, lighthouse).
- windmill: tapered Lathe tower (#F6EFE2, h 1.5) with a #9B6B43 door and a #FF6B6B cap. 4 lattice sails in #FFFFFF on the 'spin' pivot around a #FF6B6B hub. Idle speed 0.25 rev/s. On tap it spins up to 2.5 rev/s, eases back over 3 s, and plays 'whoosh'. At Showtime each sail tip carries a neon dot (pink, cyan, violet, lime) trailing a short 6-segment light streak, like a light-painting windmill.
- lighthouse: 2.8 u tapered Lathe tower in #FFFFFF with 2 #FF5C6C bands, an ink torus gallery, a lamp-room slab whose glass goes from #CFE0EC to #FFE36B when lit, and a #FF5C6C cone roof. Act 'glow': when on, 2 additive beam cones (r 0.6, length 6) rotate at 0.3 rev/s. The beam is warm #FFF6A8 by day. At Showtime it cycles Neon Pink → Cyan → Violet every 4 s like a stage spot. The body ALWAYS stays red-and-white, as the shop text says.

PATHS (path_stone, path_wood, path_flower). Flat tiles 0.03–0.05 u tall that receive shadows but never cast them, drawn as instances.
- stone: 5 flattened pebbles (puffs scaled to 0.25 in y) in #CFC8DC with a #E6E1EF highlight, laid out like the 2D tile.
- wood: 5 planks, slab(0.17, 0.04, 0.9), alternating #D69D64 and #C98F58, running front to back, with 2 ink nail dots each.
- flower stepping stones: 2 oval #D9D3E6 stones with 3 tiny flowers (#FF7AB8, #FFC93C, #FFFFFF) between them.
- SHOWTIME 'stage runway': every path tile gains an additive Neon Cyan under-glow quad at opacity 0.35. A chase-light wave runs along connected path cells (4-neighbour flood fill) at 2 cells/s, turning the paths into an LED catwalk. Off by day.

FUN ITEMS (trampoline, fountain, swing, bubbles). Each act lasts at most 3 s (the swing's decay is the exception), can be interrupted, and repeated taps never stack.
- trampoline: frame is a torus (R 0.42, r 0.05, #4B8FF0). The mat is #2A64C9 with a #7FB3FF highlight ellipse, on 3 ink bean legs. On tap the active pet runs over and does 3 bounces (0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 u high) with a front flip on the last. The mat dips 0.12 u at each contact. Sound: 'boing' 3 times with combo steps 0, 2 and 4 layered on top.
- fountain: 2-tier Lathe basin in #C9C3D9 (r 0.45 and 0.2) holding #6FD0FF water that ripples gently. Idle: 3 arcing droplet streams (12 instanced drops). On tap a 3 s water show runs: 4 jets rise in sequence (centre, left, right, then all together) like a concert fountain. At Showtime the droplets pick up neon tints. Sounds: 'whoosh', a rising combo, then 'star'.

GAME SCENE: PET COURSE 3D ('Debut Run'). The logic is untouched. Mapping is 100 logic px = 1 u: x = dist/100, y = (GROUND - y)/100, lane z = 0. Side 3/4 camera at (petX + 2.2, 1.7, 7.5) looking at (petX + 2.2, 0.9, 0), FOV 40, which puts the pet about 18% from the left, matching PET_X. Parallax: hill2 at z -6, hill at z -12, then the sky dome, plus props for each theme (meadow trees; beach palms and crabs; snow pines and snowmen; candy lollipops and cupcakes). Obstacles use the same sizes as KINDS:
- low: a hurdle
- log: a cylinder with end rings
- hedge: a slab with leaf puffs
- stack: 2–3 crates, hay bales, snow blocks or cupcakes, depending on theme
- puddle: a flat rippling ellipse (chocolate #A0522D in candy)
Treats: bone, fish (#FF8A5C) and wrapped sweet. Course stars are puffy 3D glow stars in #FFE36B with a Neon Cyan halo, so they look clearly different from the ⭐ reward icon. A bump plays a cartoon forward roll with 3 dizzy sparkles during the 0.9 s slow-down. The finish is a stage arch with confetti and fan blobs waving wands.

GAME SCENE: PENALTY 3D ('Shootout Showcase'). The goal plane is z = 0, with 1 u = 76.67 logic px: x = (lx - 480)/76.67 and y = (340 - ly)/76.67, so the goal is 6.0 × 2.48 u. Camera behind the kicker at (0, 1.4, 9.5) looking at (0, 1.1, 0), FOV 38. The kicker is the active pet with its accessories, doing a run-up and a big cartoon paw-kick, while the avatar cheers from the touchline with a wand. The keeper is an original round goalie-blob mascot: #7BD88F jersey, huge white gloves, friendly face. Its LEAN must read clearly (15° plus a raised arm), because the lean is the gameplay tell. Aim UI: the X sweep is a Neon Cyan bar and the Y sweep a Neon Pink bar, with locked glowing pins. The top corners, which always score, twinkle slowly. On a goal: the net ripples, confetti, a crowd wave and 'GOAL!'. On a save: a goofy belly-flop from the keeper and 'SAVED!', never mocking. On a miss: the ball boings off the post or floats over the bar and the text says 'So close!'.

GAME SCENE: KART 3D ('Neon Grand Prix'). Mapping is 40 logic px = 1 u, so half-width HW = 1.25 u and the walls sit at 2.75 u. The track ribbon is built once from the logic centreline (pts/tang), with kerbs, verges in the track's grass colour, and instanced wall stacks. Default chase cam: 6.5 u up, 7.5 u behind, looking 4 u ahead, FOV 50, position smoothing 1 - e^(-8dt), yaw smoothing 1 - e^(-5dt), no roll. A 'Map cam' option in the menu gives a high 3/4 view like the 2D game, for younger drivers. Driving on grass raises dust puffs and plays 'skid'. Hitting a wall is a soft squash-bounce with 'bump' and no debris. Do NOT draw boost pads or item boxes, because the logic has neither.

SHOP ICONS AND PREVIEWS (the 'photocard' renders). One shared offscreen renderer draws each id once to a 256² transparent PNG, cached by id + state + LOOK_VERSION in memory and in Cache Storage. Camera: FOV 30, elevation 28°, yaw 25° (3/4 view from the front-left), item filling 80% of the frame, Day lights, blob shadow. The detail view is a live turntable: a stage riser (r 0.7, #FFF0FA top, Neon Pink ring) with 2 crossing spot cones, turning at 0.15 rev/s (still with reduced motion). Style items preview on the player's own house and accessories on their active pet. Karts, balls and stadiums preview in a mini scene, and variants play a 2 s flythrough. Game previews run the autopilot in 3D. Without 3D, the existing SVG icons and 2D demos are used as they are.

An invalid cell is #E74C3C at 0.42, pulsing at 1.5 Hz. The entrance cell is #FFD23F at 0.25. These match the 2D CSS meanings. A picked-up item lifts 0.25 u, wobbles ±4° at 3 Hz, and its shadow shrinks to 70%; the selected item's outline turns #FFD23F. Dropping an item plays a squash-and-stretch landing with 'chip' and a dust puff. Storing an item shrinks it into a sparkle that flies to the tray.

motion:
TEMPO: island music runs at 100 BPM (beat 0.6 s) and Showtime at 118 BPM (beat 0.508 s). Idle loop periods are multiples of half a beat where possible, so the island quietly 'breathes' with the music. Nothing moves faster than 2 Hz except wings and tails.

IDLE:
- trees sway 1–3° every 3.6–5 s; flowers bob ±2% every 2.4 s
- flags and bunting flutter; the windmill turns at 0.25 rev/s; the fountain trickles; chimney smoke loops every 2.4 s; bulbs twinkle
- sea bands scroll; clouds drift at 0.08 u/s; blossom petals fall
- the avatar bobs 0.02 u at 0.5 Hz
- pets wander at 0.9 u/s (bunny in 0.18 u hops, dragon fluttering) and do an idle action every 4–8 s
- the mossy rock blinks every 5–9 s
Every loop is phase-offset by uid so nothing marches in lockstep. The dance break is the exception, where lockstep is the point.

TAP FEEDBACK: every tappable thing, even one with no act, squishes 1 → 0.92 → 1.06 → 1 over 0.25 s (outBack) with 'pop', then plays its act animation. Acts can be interrupted and never stack.

PLACE / BUY: an item drops in from 1.2 u: falls for 0.22 s (inQuad), squashes to y 0.8 and xz 1.12 for 0.08 s, then rebounds with outBack over 0.25 s. A 6-puff dust ring, plus 'chip' and 'pop'. On purchase, 'coins' plays and the item debuts on the stage riser with one 360° turn over 1.2 s, a sparkle burst and 'tada'. Purchases of 300 ⭐ or more (the confirm threshold) add confetti cannons from both screen edges and 'fanfare'.

DANCE BREAK: runs at Showtime, 8 counts at 118 BPM, about 4.1 s, then back to idle. It repeats every 16 bars while Showtime is on. Pets first walk to open cells near the house (at most 2 s), then dance in place.
- counts 1–2: side-step left and right with a 10° lean
- counts 3–4: two hops
- counts 5–6: signature moves. Puppy 'tail-wag shuffle' (hip wiggle and paw wave). Kitten 'paw point' (points up-left, then up-right). Bunny 'hop-spin'. Dragon 'wing twirl' (flutters up 0.2 u, spins, puffs sparkles). Avatar 'wand wave'.
- count 7: everyone turns to the camera
- count 8: group pose, finger-hearts or heart sprites, and a sparkle burst

CELEBRATIONS: a land unlock raises the land, sets off 3 sparkle-ring fireworks and plays applause. Reaching a goal triggers an 8 s Showtime encore. A personal best in a game shows 'NEW PERSONAL BEST!' with fireworks and a crowd wave. Finishing a game gives confetti and the pet's signature move.

CAMERA (island): PerspectiveCamera, FOV 30, for the telephoto 'toy diorama' look. The default view is 52° elevation at yaw 0, straight on, so grid editing matches the 2D map. It frames the whole unlocked island with a 6% margin and reframes smoothly when land unlocks. Controls:
- drag orbits yaw ±35° and elevation 40–65°
- pinch or wheel zooms 0.75–1.6×, with inertia damping 0.12
- double-tapping an item dollies in over 0.6 s to frame it
- a home button resets the view
Reveal moves:
- land unlock: crane from 52° to 40° toward the region over 1.4 s, hold 1.5 s, return over 1.0 s
- game launch: push in toward the attraction over 0.7 s, then fade into the game
- Showtime: slow 8° orbit over 8 s, then back
All camera moves use easeInOutSine, and the camera never rolls.

GAMES: the course camera follows with 3 u of lookahead. The penalty camera follows the ball 40% of the way, then holds. After a goal, a 1.2 s replay angle from beside the post plays (skipped under reduced motion). The kart chase cam is as specified in the item notes. Screen shake happens only on course bumps and kart wall hits: 0.06 u for 0.18 s, decaying.

REDUCED MOTION (prefers-reduced-motion OR the app's own reduced flag):
- camera moves become instant cuts, and there is no shake
- no idle sway or bob, no falling petals
- confetti physics becomes a 0.4 s sparkle fade
- the dance break becomes one group pose with a sparkle fade
- spotlights stay still, and chase lights become a steady glow
- the Showtime transition is a 0.25 s crossfade
In every mode: no flashing faster than 2 Hz and no full-screen white flash.

doAndDont: DO keep every item looking like its CATALOG name and description, because those texts show in the shop and cannot change. The red tile roof stays red tile, the lighthouse stays red-and-white, the cape is red and flaps, the scarf is stripy, the bow is spotty, the crown is golden, the thatch is fluffy straw, and the candy roof has icing and sprinkles.

DO reuse the locked 2D colours for every selectable style, cosmetic and pet (WALL, DOOR, roof pairs, PETCOL, KARTS, BALLS, STADIA, THEME, course THEMES, kart TRACKS). Old saves, the SVG fallback icons and the 3D look must all agree.
DO keep neon to emissive accents, at most 10% of the frame by day. DON'T paint walls, ground or sky in neon; that is exactly where 'tacky' begins.

DON'T use any real idol, group, label, TV show, song title, lyric, logo, fandom name, fandom colour scheme, official light-stick shape or recognisable choreography. Don't write Hangul or slogans that point to real artists, and don't prompt music 'in the style of' anyone. The K-pop flavour comes only from original staging, light, colour, sparkle, dance energy and the feel of the music.

DO build every model procedurally from the primitive kit, with textures drawn on a canvas at runtime. DON'T download or embed models, textures, HDRIs or sound files, and load no fonts beyond Bagel Fat One, Baloo 2 and Fredoka.

DO leave game logic and GAME_RULES alone. No GAME_RULES change is needed for this art direction: the 3D views only read round.state and map coordinates, so the same inputs must give the same results as the 2D games. Keep the 2D render(ctx) as the fallback.
DON'T add graphics that suggest mechanics the logic doesn't have, such as boost pads, power-ups, coins or extra lives.
DON'T let anything collectable in a game look like the ⭐ reward icon. Course stars are 3D glow stars with a cyan halo, and the line 'Game scores don't earn or spend ⭐' stays on the results screen.
DO keep every game's autopilot driving the 3D view. The shop preview plays the autopilot in 3D for 7 s on the stage riser and falls back to the 2D demo canvas.

DO make bumps and misses cartoon-funny: rolls, boings, dizzy sparkles, the keeper's goofy flop. DON'T show injury, damage, debris, fire, explosions, crying, scary faces, darkness or loud bangs. The dragon puffs sparkles and the volcano is cute and never erupts.
DO honour reduced motion fully, as set out in the motion section. NEVER flash faster than 2 Hz or flash the full screen white in any mode (photosensitivity).

DO keep all real UI in HTML: aria labels, keyboard focus and the #FFD23F focus ring. The canvas is a visual layer with raycast taps, backed by a hidden list of placed items that keyboard users can focus.
DO keep silhouettes distinct at 48 px icon size and readable from the default 52° camera. Check each item beside its neighbours on the grid.
DO keep placement easy to read: decor stays inside 0.86 × 0.86 of its cell, only tree canopies overhang, and buildings, attractions, paths and fun items are never jittered.
DON'T make spending feel like a game of chance. Shine levels follow price only and are deterministic: no random rewards, loot boxes, spin wheels, countdown timers or 'limited time' pressure.
DON'T autoplay audio before a tap, and DON'T play music on learning screens. DO duck music under big sound effects.
DO judge the art on the LOW tier first, on an older iPad, in both Day and Showtime. It must look good with no shadow map and no outlines before any polish is added.
DO put per-item look data in a pure module that Node can test, plus a test that every CATALOG id has a look entry built only from palette or locked tokens.
DON'T use realistic humans. The only person on the island is the chibi avatar, whose face is the child's own emoji. Crowds are original fan blobs.
DO fall back silently to the existing 2D island and games on any WebGL or CDN failure, a lost context, or sustained frame rates under 20 fps. The child should never see an error.
DON'T use parts thinner than 0.02 u (they shimmer at low pixel ratios), tiny text inside textures, or more than 3 overlapping transparent layers (fill-rate is limited on iPads).
performanceBudget:
TARGET: 60 fps on a 2019-era iPad (A10/A12 chip) and on mid-range Android phones, never dropping below 30 fps.

TIERS: decide the tier BEFORE creating the renderer, because antialias cannot be changed afterwards.
- LOW: iOS or Android with hardwareConcurrency ≤ 4, or gl MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE < 8192, or a LOW tier saved from an earlier session
- HIGH: a desktop without touch and with hardwareConcurrency ≥ 8
- MID: everything else
Save the measured tier per device in localStorage, wrapped in try/catch.

PIXEL RATIO CAP: LOW 1.0, MID min(dpr, 1.5), HIGH min(dpr, 2). Antialias on MID and HIGH only.

DRAW CALLS, everything on screen:
- island: ≤ 70 LOW, 100 MID, 150 HIGH
- games: ≤ 60, 90, 120
How: InstancedMesh per (id, material) for repeatables, mergeGeometries per material for unique items, one particle InstancedMesh and one halo InstancedMesh.

TRIANGLES ON SCREEN:
- island: ≤ 60k LOW, 120k MID, 200k HIGH
- games: ≤ 50k, 100k, 150k

SHADER PROGRAMS: at most 12 (toon+rim, basic, basic-additive, matcap, water, sky, cones, points, outline, shadow depth, sprite). Precompile them with renderer.compile(scene, camera) behind the loading veil so the first tap doesn't stutter.

TEXTURES: all generated on a canvas at runtime, at most 8 MB of GPU memory in total:
- toon gradient 4×1; halo, twinkle and blob textures at 64² each
- 4 matcaps at 128²; one 128² emoji face per child
- banner text 512×128; shore-distance map 64×40
- LED board 256×64, animated by UV offset and never redrawn per frame

LIGHTS: 1 hemisphere plus 1 directional. Zero PointLights or SpotLights; glows and beams are faked. Shadows use the static map (autoUpdate false): 1024² on MID, 2048² on HIGH, none on LOW (blob shadows instead).

PARTICLES: one pooled quad InstancedMesh with capacity 128 LOW, 256 MID, 512 HIGH. Limits: confetti ≤ 120 alive, bubbles ≤ 24, petals ≤ 40, snow ≤ 60 / 100 / 150.

CPU: view updates take ≤ 4 ms per frame on the target iPad, with zero allocations inside the frame loop (reuse Vector3, Matrix4 and Color). Only animated instances get matrix updates; statics are never touched after placement. Raycast only on pointer events, and only against hit boxes.

FRAME PACING: use setAnimationLoop.
- Drop to 30 fps after 20 s with no input, and return to 60 on the next input.
- Stop rendering completely while document.hidden is true, while the island view is closed or scrolled out of view (IntersectionObserver), and while a game or the shop sheet covers the island.
- Under reduced motion, when nothing is animating, render on demand only.

ADAPTIVE QUALITY: keep a rolling 120-frame average. If it stays above 24 ms for 2 s, step down one level at a time:
1. pixel ratio -0.25
2. shadows off
3. outlines off
4. particle counts halved
5. Showtime cones off
Never step back up during a session. If frame rates stay under 20 fps after every step, or webglcontextlost fires twice, switch to the 2D SVG island and canvas games for this session and remember the choice.

LOADING: show the existing 2D island immediately. Load three plus only BufferGeometryUtils and RoundedBoxGeometry from jsDelivr in the background (the service worker caches them), then crossfade to 3D over 300 ms once the first frame is ready. If 3D isn't ready within 8 s, or the CDN or WebGL2 fails, stay on 2D silently. Target ≤ 1.5 s from opening to 3D on a cached load. Build item geometry lazily on first use and cache it by id + state + tier.

MEMORY: dispose geometries, materials and textures when leaving the island. One shared offscreen renderer makes the shop icons and is disposed once its queue is empty. Game scenes are fully disposed on exit through the shell's round.dispose().
